items.title: Byron Stripling interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 25, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Thad Jones, I’ll just talk about him quickly, was like a father to me. I’ve followed him around like a little puppy.

ctx.x: And Thad Jones was conducting at that time?

Yeah actually I got there at a pivotal period. I got there right when Basie had died. And then Eric Dixon was the conductor. I don’t know if you know Eric but he was a great tenor player in the band. He was Straw Boss during the later years. And it’s a great sort of lesson about, I don’t know if it’s too trivial to tell on the tape, but a lesson about sort of business. It’s always nice to observe stuff. Basie died and the guys said we want to keep the band going, let’s try to keep it going. Eric Dixon is Straw…

prices went up and the band was able to survive. Because see they didn’t cut anybody’s salary, they just kept it, so you’ve got to keep a consistent thing coming in, and Thad did very well for the band. And for me it was like I was in heaven. Thad Jones, I’ll just talk about him quickly, was like a father to me. I’ve followed him around like a little puppy. Because there are certain people I think that are born leaders. It’s like they’re put here, okay, you’re going to be a leader. And he was one of those people.…

items.title: Byron Stripling interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 25, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I remember myself seeing that band a lot.

ctx.x: it’s pre-Covid. I don’t know if this pandemic should actually affect what you tell students yet. That was a long phrased question, but —

Oh no. It’s a great question. First of all actually what I had to discuss with my father was even better than what you described. He would say, “I know you were at Carnegie Hall last night” and I appreciated it. He and my mother. And I know that you played on a record date and you know, I was so lucky when I lived in New York, I was doing so much. What I would say to kids about that part of your life to and explaining it to your parents is, those challenges are good. It’s good to be able to defend what you’re…

that’s jazz and that’s, you know, but anyway Dick had that same vision of going to New York and making it and that was his first night. Certain people aren’t so lucky. I walked into New York and I had a Broadway show when I decided to permanently move there. Certainly I can talk to you about other things people can do and in fact in regard to what people should do now as opposed to before Covid or after, the music is still going to be there. It’s still going to be great music, but we have to adapt ourselves to…
